messages:
sara: Heads-up — drafting a short 'spot evacuation + oncall handoff' checklist we can pin to eng-infra. Trying to keep it ~8 bullets for paging situations.

mike: +1, please include graceful preemption window and where to find checkpoint endpoints.

sara: Draft below — please edit inline:

sara: 1) Assess scope: check `spot_reclaim_rate` dashboard + 'gpu-preemptions' panel in console.

sara: 2) Signal threshold: if reclaim spikes >10% over 5m, start evacuation protocol (adjust by cluster criticality).

julia: Suggest: use 5% for prod-critical clusters, 10% for dev. Also note region-specific tolerances (e.g., us-east-1b historically noisier).

sara: 3) Quick commands (taint first, then drain):

sara: ```bash
# prevent new pods
kubectl taint nodes <node> spot-evacuate=true:NoSchedule
# evict pods, keep daemonsets, allow longer grace for stateful jobs
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120
```

mike: Remember to set `--grace-period` high enough for checkpoint flushes. We default to 120s for short jobs, 600s for long-running encoders.

sara: 4) Cache handling: promote caches to read-only replicas, and trigger KV copy to fallback Redis cluster: `scripts/kv-failover.sh --target redis-fallback`. Verify TTLs and eviction policy.

ops_bot: [automated note] Evacuation protocol started by sara. Posting incident stub to tracker and notifying #eng-infra.

leo: 5) Routing: switch inference traffic to fallback route `evac-fallback` that uses smaller models or replicated inference lanes with prewarmed CPU instances. Use Console > Routing to trigger.

julia: 6) Escalation: if >20% of GPU capacity lost OR SLO error rate increases >30% for 10m, page @ops_lead and infra-scheduling. Include short summary + links.

sara: 7) Cost guardrail check: if spot preemption saves <10% vs reserved for the current billing period, abort further spot use and start reserved burst (see reserved-burst playbook).

mike: 8) Handoff note template (leave this in thread for next oncall):

sara: ```
Handoff started: 1765009876
Nodes drained: gpu-usw2-03,gpu-usw2-07
Affected services: inference-v2,batch-encoder
Checkpoint status: batch-encoder snapshot succeeded (s3://snapshots/enc-1765), inference caches copying to fallback Redis (in progress)
Actions taken: tainted + drained nodes, switched routing to evac-fallback, notified infra-scheduling
Followups: verify all snapshots, consider reserved burst in us-west2 if reclaim persists
```

julia: Can someone attach the monitoring panels link here? I'll pin it after review.

sara: Dashboards: https://console.internal/dashboards/spot-preemptions and https://console.internal/dashboards/gpu-health

ops_lead: Love this. Add an explicit "abort evacuation" subsection: how to revert taints, uncordon nodes, and validate cluster stability.

sara: Abort commands: `kubectl uncordon <node>` and remove taint label: `kubectl taint nodes <node> spot-evacuate-`. Then check `kubectl get pods -o wide` and routing policies.

mike: I'll convert this into a short Confluence playbook and add a 15-min runthrough to next oncall training. Also will add automation to `ops_bot` to post the handoff template automatically when evacuation is triggered.

sara: Thanks all — tagging @julia @leo for final review. :wave: Please add any region-specific notes (e.g., gcp preempt pattern in asia-south1).
